mission.display_title: Generate RVs with the inverse transform method

mission.learning_objective: Generate basic discrete and continuous random variables using the inverse transform method.
mission.concept_focus: U~Uniform(0,1) → invert CDF / use discrete inverse → generated draw; refuse black-box theatre.
mission.prior_bridge: Yesterday's Poisson process connection used families you already evaluate. Today applies generation method 2.1.5. Still topic 2.1.
mission.why_now: Inverse transform is the syllabus method LO before software-generation practice (2.1.6).

knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: inverse transform steps
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly lists the inverse-transform steps for a continuous random variable with CDF F?
knowledge_checks.body: Select Uniform source plus inverse CDF.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Method fluency requires naming Uniform(0,1) and applying the inverse CDF.

choices.label: Draw U ~ Uniform(0,1). Set X = F^{-1}(U), the quantile function. Then X has CDF F under standard conditions.
Draw X directly from F without a Uniform source, because the inverse CDF step is optional.
Draw U ~ Normal(0,1) and set X = F(U), using the CDF rather than the inverse CDF.
Set X = F(U) with U already equal to X, which makes Uniform sampling unnecessary.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: discrete case + refuse black-box
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly outlines discrete inverse-transform sampling and refuses a software-only substitute for the method?
knowledge_checks.body: Choose discrete outline plus method warrant.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: 2.1.5 is method competence; software alone does not satisfy the learning objective.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Discrete: Uniform then CDF threshold. Refuse treating a sampler call as a substitute for the method.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Only saying use rbinom without the inverse idea.

choices.label: Draw U ~ Uniform(0,1) and assign the discrete value whose CDF first exceeds U (inverse CDF or threshold rule). Software sampling can implement the draw, but the learning objective requires understanding inverse transform, not only calling a black box.
For discrete variables, skip Uniform and thresholds and only call a sampler such as rbinom, because software replaces the method.
Discrete inverse transform uses Normal draws rather than Uniform, and understanding the method is optional once a library exists.
Assign outcomes by sorting probabilities alphabetically with no Uniform threshold, which finishes the inverse-transform LO.
